source: Weekly refresh by Claude (scheduled task). Edit freely; the next refresh replaces this file.

items.title: Send-worthy reels: make one reel people would DM to a friend
items.why: Instagram now weighs DM sends more than likes when showing reels to new people.
items.tip: End with a line like 'send this to the friend who always shoots on their phone'.

items.title: Longer story-led reel (1 to 3 minutes) of a full shoot day
items.why: Longer reels that hold attention are outperforming the old 15 to 30 second clips.
items.tip: Hook in the first 3 seconds, then keep shots under 3 seconds each.

items.title: Trial reel test: post a hook variation to non-followers first
items.why: Trial Reels show to non-followers first, so you can test hooks without spamming your followers.
items.tip: Compare watch time to your average before sharing it to everyone.

items.title: How I got the shot: BTS reel with camera settings on screen
items.why: Educational and behind the scenes content makes up most of what performs for creators.
items.tip: Show the phone BTS clip, then cut to the final image.

items.title: Captioned reel that works with the sound off
items.why: Most viewers watch muted, so on-screen text keeps them watching.
items.tip: Bold text in the first frame doubles as your hook.

items.title: Before and after colour grade carousel
items.why: Transformation content is one of the most reliable formats for photographers.
items.tip: Put the after first so the cover image is your best frame.

items.title: Year-end function teaser for caterers and venues
items.why: November and December are peak event season in South Africa.
items.tip: Tag the venue and caterer so they reshare.

items.title: Client collab post (Instagram Collab) after every shoot
items.why: Collab posts show on both accounts and act as social proof for new leads.
items.tip: Send the invite the same day you deliver the gallery.
